column1: # BASE/icon2bc typed command and loop-state abstraction pass, checkpoint 08966f9

# Target: IconToBitmapColorTable, RVA 0xd32a0, retail size 0x5af, target object SHA-256 a37407754627bc06241364dbb769148a02223a8e05bee63d57bebfa3b43d4f82, target .text SHA-256 15096a6b70e855d536084307e3f0f9caff5f35f7da2c157ef2fe1a80feeb647c, target relocations 91.

# New evidence: retail Icon2b and icon2bc share the same setup register sequence (data=ESI, 13*frame=EBX, entry.x=ECX, srcOffset=EAX, entry=EDI), and icon2bc carries destination=EBX across every command backedge. This pass tested typed abstractions for those shared roles, not another file-static scratch-record boundary or a local fetch spelling.
# No regex or AST permutation tool was used. All rejected types/headers were removed; canonical 73.1690/0x566/88:91 is restored.

column5: Separate typed table plus scalar command and loop-header destination reload; first divergence +0x12. Missing ClipR/Cnt/Dst/X0 once each and excess Y once.

Inline frame-byte-offset, frame-X, source-offset, and entry accessors recover retail EBX=13*frame at +0x11, but allocate frame-X=EDI and entry=ECX instead of retail ECX/EDI. Predeclaring entry is byte-identical; a short frame-X is 67.38 and extending X ownership is 67.41.
A typed reference alias for the global source plus the retail pre-loop destination lifetime still emits source=EAX, command=ECX, destination=EDX, count=EBX and loses five occurrences.

A scalar class with inline command classification/run-length methods makes MSVC lay out the positive body before the negative body (JL at the command split), unlike retail's JGE-to-positive shape. Returning raw signed/bits values does not restore the CFG.
One inline decoder object owns every command/payload read and the extended-solid/dim length decodes. The source remains EAX and command ECX; the abstraction shortens and reorders branch bodies.
Combining the same full run decoder with the retail destination lifetime retains destination=EDX/count=EBX and does not recover the five occurrence signature.
A header-level command enum restores every relocation occurrence but retains source=EAX/command=ECX and broadly regresses instruction selection.
The enum plus loop-carried destination remains destination=EDX/count=EBX and loses four occurrences.
A header-level dim/override flag domain restores all occurrences but changes comparison polarity and addressing throughout fill/dim.
Keeping int storage while using a header-level typedef-enum constant domain preserves the canonical occurrence delta but perturbs row formation and later allocation.
A one-field local destination-cursor record declared after icon.h remains destination=EDX and changes setup/row allocation.
Moving the same real loop-state type to icon2bc.h changes initial clip CSE but still emits source=EAX, command=ECX, destination=EDX, count=EBX.

column1: # Result: neither an inline frame view, a command value object, a cursor-backed full run decoder, semantic command/flags enum types, nor a one-word typed destination state explains the retail allocation. The full-decoder abstraction is observably worse than the already-recorded scalar source, and the typed enum surfaces prove that matching all 91 occurrences alone is insufficient.

# Revisit trigger: a new retail-backed abstraction must account for the simultaneous ECX-source/EAX-command/EDX-count/EBX-destination allocation without changing the JGE negative/positive split, or a real shared header/compiler-state change. Do not retry these type placements or wrap only the command/payload reader again.
